title: Dualizing unit and composite tensor identifications
statement:
Fix the field $k$ and finite coefficient ring $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ ($n\ge1$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$) of [def-pur-conventions]. All schemes are finite-type $k$-schemes, with no absolute separatedness assumption, and all morphisms are separated and finite type [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Work on $D^b_{ctf}$ on the small pro-etale sites, with pullback and tensor [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], the constructible exceptional inverse image [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], and the specified compactification projection, counit and tensor transpose $\theta_{a,K}$ [def-exchange-projection, def-pur-co-smoothness]. Put $W_a=Ra^!A$ and let $c_{b,a}:R(ba)^!\xrightarrow{\sim}Ra^!Rb^!$ be the conjugate of the compact-support compositor [thm-sf-comp-composition, def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]. For any composable $a:X\to Y$, $b:Y\to Z$, define
$$\sigma_{a,b}=c_{b,a,A}^{-1}\circ\theta_{a,W_b}\circ\mathrm{sym}:W_a\otimes^LLa^*W_b\longrightarrow W_{ba}.$$

For every $a$, $\theta_{a,A}$ is the canonical map $La^*A\otimes^LW_a\cong W_a$, with the coefficient-unit pullback comparison inserted. If $b$ has any isomorphism $\eta:W_b\xrightarrow{\sim}A_Y$, set
$$t_{a,\eta}=\operatorname{unitor}\circ(1_{W_a}\otimes La^*\eta):W_a\otimes^LLa^*W_b\xrightarrow{\sim}W_a.$$
Then $\sigma_{a,b}$ is invertible and its inverse, after this specified identification of its source with $W_a$, is
$$t_{a,\eta}\circ\sigma_{a,b}^{-1}=Ra^!(\eta)\circ c_{b,a,A}:W_{ba}\longrightarrow W_a.$$
In addition suppose a morphism $e:U\to X$ has a natural isomorphism $\rho_e:Re^!\xrightarrow{\sim}Le^*$, put $\eta_e=\rho_{e,A}$ with the coefficient-unit comparison, and assume
$$\rho_{e,K}\theta_{e,K}=\operatorname{unitor}(1\otimes\eta_e)$$
for every $K$ in the stated category. For every composable $h:X\to S$, put $E_{e,h}=\rho_{e,W_h}c_{h,e,A}$. Then
$$E_{e,h}\sigma_{e,h}=\operatorname{unitor}(\eta_e\otimes1):W_e\otimes^LLe^*W_h\longrightarrow Le^*W_h,$$
and $\sigma_{e,h}$ is invertible. All these formulas are natural under compatible restriction of the given operation, tensor, counit and composition data to open subschemes. No smoothness, orientation or Tate twist is required.

proof.text: Write $F=Ra_!$, $G=Ra^!$, $P=La^*$ and $W=GA$. Work at the specified compactification $a=pj$. The proper projection of [def-exchange-projection] is the counit-defined map of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]; its last assertion says that its component at $A$ is the identity after unit identifications. For the open factor, [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] specifies the inverse of $\gamma_{M,N}$ as the $j_!\dashv j^*$-adjunct of $u_M\otimes1$. At $N=A$, the tensor unit identifications turn this adjunct into $u_M$. The identity of $j_!M$ has the same adjunct, so $\gamma_{M,A}$ is the identity under the unit identifications. Composing these two factors in the displayed definition of $\operatorname{PF}^c$ gives $\operatorname{PF}^c_{a,M,A}=1_{FM}$ after inserting $PA\simeq A$ and the unitors. No absolute separatedness is used: the proper-factor lemma applies to any ringed topos morphism and the open-factor lemma to any open immersion.

proof.text: Use the specified transpose of [def-pur-co-smoothness] and the adjunction of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. At $K=A$, Step 1 removes $\operatorname{PF}^{-1}$; the symmetry and unitors turn its defining adjunct into $\varepsilon_{a,A}:FW\to A$, preceded by $F$ of the canonical map $PA\otimes W\to W$. The adjunct of $\varepsilon_{a,A}$ is $1_W$, by the adjunction triangle identity. Naturality of the adjunction bijection in the source therefore identifies $\theta_{a,A}$ with that canonical map. This proves the first clause with the actual coefficient-unit pullback comparison.

source.place: Step 1: etale normalization; explicit tensor-unit and naturality calculation

proof.text:
For the naturality calculation put $q_K: F(PK\otimes W)\to K$ equal to the adjunct defining $\theta_{a,K}$ in [def-pur-co-smoothness]. The finite projection theorem [lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula] gives natural invertible projection maps on precisely these finite-Tor inputs. Thus, for $v:K\to L$, inverse-projection naturality and tensor symmetry give
$$q_L\circ F(Pv\otimes1_W)=v\circ q_K.$$
Indeed the inverse-projection square moves $v$ to $1_{FW}\otimes v$, and $(\varepsilon_{a,A}\otimes1)$ then gives $\varepsilon_{a,A}\otimes v$ on either path; the final unitors are natural. Apply the natural Hom bijection of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] to get
$$G(v)\circ\theta_{a,K}=\theta_{a,L}\circ(Pv\otimes1_W).$$
This uses only naturality of the specified projection and the defining transpose, with no hypothesis that $a$ is cohomologically smooth.

source.place: Step 1: etale normalization; explicit tensor-unit and naturality calculation

proof.text: The compact-support compositor is a natural isomorphism by [thm-sf-comp-composition]. Conjugation sends an isomorphism to an isomorphism by [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]. Hence the specified $c_{b,a,A}:W_{ba}\to G(W_b)$ is invertible. This uses only the compositor and its right-adjoint conjugate, not a smooth-purity identification.

source.place: Step 1: etale normalization; explicit tensor-unit and naturality calculation

proof.text:
Apply Step 3 with $v=\eta:W_b\xrightarrow{\sim}A_Y$, then Step 2, and precompose by the tensor symmetry $s:W\otimes PW_b\to PW_b\otimes W$. Cancellation of $c$ in the definition of $\sigma$ gives
$$G(\eta)c_{b,a,A}\sigma_{a,b}=G(\eta)\theta_{a,W_b}s=\theta_{a,A}(P\eta\otimes1_W)s=\operatorname{unitor}(1_W\otimes P\eta)=t_{a,\eta}.$$
The last equality is naturality of symmetry followed by its unit constraint. Both $G(\eta)c_{b,a,A}$ and $t_{a,\eta}$ are isomorphisms: functors preserve an inverse, and tensoring the maps $P\eta$ and $P\eta^{-1}$ gives mutually inverse maps. Consequently $\sigma_{a,b}=(G(\eta)c_{b,a,A})^{-1}t_{a,\eta}$ is invertible. Postcomposing the displayed equality by $\sigma_{a,b}^{-1}$ proves exactly $t_{a,\eta}\sigma_{a,b}^{-1}=G(\eta)c_{b,a,A}$. In particular no special normalization of the arbitrary isomorphism $\eta$ has been imposed.

source.place: Step 1: etale normalization; explicit tensor-unit and naturality calculation

proof.text:
For the additional hypotheses on $e$, write $s:W_e\otimes Le^*W_h\to Le^*W_h\otimes W_e$ for symmetry. Expand the two specified maps and cancel $c_{h,e,A}c_{h,e,A}^{-1}$:
$$E_{e,h}\sigma_{e,h}=\rho_{e,W_h}\theta_{e,W_h}s=\operatorname{unitor}(1\otimes\eta_e)s=\operatorname{unitor}(\eta_e\otimes1).$$
The middle equality is precisely the assumed equation at $K=W_h$; the last is naturality of symmetry and the unit constraint. The final map is invertible since $\eta_e$ is an isomorphism, and $E_{e,h}$ is invertible by Step 4 and the assumed natural isomorphism $\rho_e$. Hence $\sigma_{e,h}$ is invertible as well. Neither $h$ nor $e$ has been assumed smooth or oriented.

proof.text: For a restriction satisfying the compatibility required in the statement, apply the restriction functor to each displayed equality. It preserves compositions and identities; the image of an inverse is the inverse of the image since both inverse equations are preserved. The stipulated compatibilities identify the restricted $P,F,G$, coefficient-unit comparisons, tensor symmetry, unitors, projections, counits and $c$ with their restricted data. They also carry $P\eta$, $G\eta$, $\rho_e$ and its normalization equation to the corresponding restricted maps. Thus Steps 1--6 become the same equations for the restrictions. This proves the claimed naturality for compatible open restriction; it does not assert the existence of an additional comparison not supplied in that compatibility hypothesis.
